title: Reduce Console Observability to Minimal MVP for Q2
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: The Console Observability epic has grown beyond team capacity for the Q2 delivery window. We need to reduce scope across dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdowns so we can ship a stable, usable surface that meets customer needs while deferring lower-priority capabilities. This ticket captures the scoped MVP, rationale for cuts, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and rollout plan. Rationale: shipping earlier with a smaller, reliable surface reduces risk for enterprise customers (Dedicated/Private) who requested stable metrics and basic tracing; it also unlocks user feedback to guide prioritized follow-up work. Trade-offs: we omit advanced multi-tenant filtering, long-term retention UI, and per-token cost anomaly detection from MVP; these will be delivered in follow-up milestones. Engineering asks for clear acceptance criteria and API contracts to avoid rework.
scope_included: Per-route latency and error rate dashboard (7-day and 30-day presets)
Token-level cost summary aggregated daily and by model (top-line numbers + 95th percentile cost per route)
Trace view for high-latency requests: single-request call stack + model variant and region metadata
Basic rollouts dashboard: current canary percentage and recent errors by rollout
Export links to raw logs/trace IDs for deeper debugging (links to existing logging infra)
scope_excluded: Interactive flamegraphs and full span-level visualization
Custom dashboard builder for arbitrary query composition
Automated anomaly detection surfaces (alerting and suggested root causes)
acceptance_criteria: Dashboards: Per-route latency/error dashboard exists in Console and shows results for seeded test routes with synthetic traffic; QA verifies correct aggregation for 7d and 30d presets
Cost summary: Daily aggregated cost numbers and 95th percentile per-route cost are visible for last 14 days; numbers match backend billing dataset within 2%
Tracing: Selecting a high-latency sample shows a trace with request metadata (model, region, model-variant), and clicking the trace opens the raw trace ID in logging system
Rollouts dashboard: Current rollout percent and error delta (compared to baseline) shown for the active canary; PM/Eng validate using canary simulation harness
Performance: Console pages load under 1.5s on 75th percentile for internal staging environment with 3s backend latency emulated
Security & Privacy: No customer PII is surfaced in dashboard or trace UIs; security sign-off obtained and automated checks pass
Docs: Updated Console docs page describing MVP observability surface, known limitations, and links to follow-up tickets
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated rollout in staging behind feature flag. 2) Internal dogfood for 1 week with Platform and Support teams. 3) Canary release to 5 pilot customers (sales-run lists) for 2 weeks; collect feedback and telemetry. 4) Gradual ramp to GA with opt-in by default for new orgs. Rollback plan: feature flag off; console falls back to legacy minimal metrics. Communication: customer-facing changelog and targeted emails to pilots.
